Senses.Explanation: The white ox in the open ground. Changqing Da'an describes a water buffalo he tended during thirty years at Guishan, repeatedly pulling it back from crops until it changed into this white ox, plainly present and no longer needing to be driven. Other named speakers keep the animal imagery active: it grows horns, must not eat another's seedlings, bellows when Linji Yixuan asks about it, is cooked for a year-end communal meal, or has nowhere to be placed when snow makes everything one color. Chan thus uses the open-ground white ox as a publicly handled figure of an animal no longer straying or concealed, while interview answers and seasonal talks keep testing whether that description has become another object to possess.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X80/X80n1565.xml). Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元): Shitou Xiqian answers the unnamed monastic by saying to ask the exposed pillar, then says he understands even less.

Senses.Explanation: The exposed pillar is a bare structural post that the records address, point questioners toward, make speak, and make bear offspring. It has 3,067 exact hits in 351 files representing 346 independent works. Guangxiao Huijue greets a pillar with joined palms as 'World-Honored One'; when an unnamed questioner says, 'Master, that is an exposed pillar,' Guangxiao answers with a verse about crying blood to no use. Shitou answers 'what is the meaning of coming from the west?' with 'ask the exposed pillar'; when the questioner cannot understand, Shitou says he understands even less. Asked to whom his teaching will be entrusted after his death, Dasui Fazhen answers 'exposed pillar, fire stove' and reverses the pair after the follow-up. Lingyun Zhiqin compares the impossible situation in a question to 'an exposed pillar bearing a child.' Guizong Zhichang says oxhide is stretched over the pillar, the pillar cries out, ordinary ears do not hear it, and the sages laugh. The Zen deviation is concrete and institutional: a fixed hall support becomes a named interlocutor, recipient, speaker, and pregnant figure in encounters, commonly partnered with lantern or stove. These are the corpus's recorded actions; the entry adds no symbolic meaning.

Senses.Explanation: A bare structural pillar is pregnant—an impossible conception used as a spoken case-image. Lingyun Zhiqin answers a question about before chaos divided with the pregnant pillar. Hongzhi Zhengjue pairs its pregnancy with a stone woman speaking, while Tianyin Yuanxiu makes it smile and nod. Tianan Guangsheng answers an unnamed monk’s demand for its meaning by saying its belly is swollen. Shiyu Mingfang publicly asks what conditions could produce this sign. Tianran Hanshi supplies the needed restraint: such images must not simply be declared existent or nonexistent, real or unreal. Zen makes the inanimate support perform conception in a public answer, question, or verse. The corpus keeps the impossibility operational without turning the entry into natural history or furnishing one fixed resolution.
